name: Telecom of Kosovo Core Telecom / IT Data Center
real_location: Pristina, Kosovo (de facto Republic of Kosovo, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 XK, ITU +383)
country_should_be: XK (de facto) / RS only if DB deliberately follows Serbian de-jure naming
reason: Facility is Telecom of Kosovo (PTK / Vala), headquartered in Pristina. Kosovo is de facto an independent state (ISO code XK, own telecom regulator ARKEP, +383 dialing) but Serbia de jure claims it as its autonomous province 'Kosovo and Metohija'. Declared country RS with subnational 'Kosovo-Metohija' reflects the Serbian administrative viewpoint; whether this is a country mismatch depends on the DB's political-coding convention (compare: DB codes facilities in the PRC SARs variously CN/HK, and elsewhere uses de facto codes). Not a clear-cut location error, but the coding is politically dependent and should be harmonized.
evidence: Wikipedia 'Telecom of Kosovo': HQ Pristina, Kosovo, subsidiary of PTK; Mapcarta 'vala - Kosovo Telecom' located in Pristina District, Kosovo; mcc-mnc.org lists MCC 221 MNC 01 as 'Telecom of Kosovo J.S.C. (Vala)' with country Kosovo; ARKEP (Kosovo regulator) oversees Vala.

name: Bitfury Norway data center (Mo Industripark)
real_location: Mo i Rana, Nordland county, Norway
reason: Country NO matches the real location: the Bitfury mining/data center is at Mo Industripark in Mo i Rana, Norway. However the subnational field 'Northland' is not a Norwegian region - Northland is a region of New Zealand; the correct Norwegian county is 'Nordland'. Likely a data-entry/translation error in the subnational field only; flagged so it can be corrected (no country change needed).
evidence: NRK (nrk.no/nordland) on Bitfury Norway data center at Mo Industripark, Mo i Rana; Mo Industripark (mip.no) press release 'Internasjonal gigant etablerer Norges storste datasenter i Mo Industripark'; Zycrypto: Bitfury $35M Bitcoin mining datacenter in Mo i Rana, Northern Norway (Nordland).
